greeting: Make it brief, Inspector. I have cables to answer, and {victim} is beyond any help of mine.
{Victim.full}. Dead. Regrettable, and inconvenient. Ask your questions.
I assume you'll want my movements. I assume, too, that you'll be quick about it.
A death aboard ship is bad for everyone's business, Inspector. Mine included. Proceed.
I did not care for {victim}, and I shan't pretend otherwise. That is not the same as wishing {victim.object} dead.
Sit down if you must. I'll give you five minutes, which is four more than I gave my last board meeting.
whereabouts: {RoomName}, {time}. I keep to a schedule, Inspector.
{RoomName}. {Time}, or near enough. I don't carry a stopwatch.
{Time}, I was {room}. That is all there is to it.
You'll find I was {room} {time}. Next question.
sawOne: {Other} was there. I paid no attention.
Only {other}, which hardly counts as company.
I saw {other}. We did not speak. We seldom do.
{Other}. {Other.subject} saw me too, I expect, if {other.subject} was paying attention.
{Other} was present. I didn't come aboard to make friends.
sawSeveral: {Others} were there. Not one of them worth the fare.
I saw {others}. I spoke to none of them.
{Others}, all talking at once. I ignored them.
There were {others}. Count them yourself if you doubt me.
{Others}. Don't expect me to vouch for any of them.
sawVictim: {Victim} was there. Alive, and as tiresome as ever.
I saw {victim}. {Victim.subject} seemed perfectly well. That is the last I can tell you about {victim.object}.
{Victim} was there, yes. We exchanged a look. Not a friendly one.
Yes, {victim}. Had I known it was the last time, I'd have been more civil. Possibly.
{Victim} was there. If you're asking whether {victim.subject} looked worried: no.
I saw {victim}. Make of that what you will.
sawNoOne: No one. I prefer it that way.
Nobody. Solitude is the only luxury on this ship worth the price.
I saw no one, and no one saw me. I imagine that's inconvenient for you.
No one. I was thinking, Inspector. Some of us do.
Nobody at all. Is that a crime aboard the Meridian?
confrontCrack: {Witness} said that, did {witness.subject}? Very well. Since you insist on being tiresome.
I see {witness} has been talking. Then you may as well have the truth, and keep it to yourself.
Damn {witness}. Close the door, Inspector. This goes no further.
Hm. I underestimated {witness}. A rare mistake. All right.
confrontDeflect: {Witness} is mistaken. People frequently are, in my experience.
You'd take the word of {witness} over mine? Then you're a poorer judge than I took you for.
{Witness} saw what {witness.subject} wanted to see. My answer stands.
I've nothing to add. If {witness} has a better memory than mine, let {witness.object} prove it.
accusedWrongly: Me? With {weapon}? My lawyers will have your pension, Inspector.
I didn't kill {victim}. I'd have had someone else do it, and done it properly.
You've made a costly error, and I always collect on those.
Absurd. You have a theory and no proof, and I've ruined better men for less.
accusedRightly: {Weapon}. Clumsy of me to leave it where I did. Yes. I killed {victim}.
Very well. {Victim} knew things about my affairs that would have finished me in New York. I made a business decision.
I don't expect you to understand. {Victim.subject} was a liability, and I have always dealt with liabilities.
Congratulations, Inspector. First man to outmanoeuvre me in twenty years. Yes: {roomName}, {weapon}, and I don't regret it.
opinion.folder: Folder? A clerk with a ledger and ideas above his station.
{Other} counts things. Spoons, tips, other people's money. I'd keep an eye on {other.object}.
{Other} has been looking at me oddly since Southampton. I don't care to be looked at oddly.
opinion.mallet: Miss Mallet knocks small balls through hoops for a living. I'm told that's a profession now.
{Other} has opinions, and a very loud voice to carry them in.
{Other.subject} dislikes me. The feeling is entirely mutual, and considerably better informed.
opinion.bear: Mrs Bear has buried one husband and is shopping for another. I am not for sale. Not at her prices.
{Other} is loud, rich and relentless. Two of those I can respect.
{Other.subject} talks. Constantly. Somewhere in all that talking, occasionally, there is money.
opinion.egg: The Egg girl? The one with the notebook. She jumps whenever I enter a room.
{Other} writes things down. I find that a deeply unattractive habit in a fellow passenger.
Harmless, I should think. Most people who apologise that often are.
opinion.pail: The steward? Adequate. Overfamiliar. Expects to be tipped for breathing.
{Other} knows every corridor on this ship. Draw your own conclusions.
I don't notice stewards, Inspector. That is rather the point of them.
eulogy.folder: Folder's dead? Then someone has saved the Line a salary.
I can't say I'll miss {other.object}. {Other.subject} looked at my bills as if they were confessions.
{Other} kept records. I should find out what happened to them, if I were you.
eulogy.mallet: Miss Mallet. Forthright to the end, I imagine. It must have been a short argument.
I didn't like {other.object}. But {other.subject} was honest, which is rarer on this ship than you'd think.
{Other.subject} would have won that tournament. A waste.
eulogy.bear: Mrs Bear. Well. The ship will be considerably quieter.
{Other.subject} had money and no sense, and someone has taken advantage of one or the other.
I won't pretend to grief, Inspector. But I wouldn't have wished it on {other.object}.
eulogy.egg: The Egg girl? Good God. Who would bother?
{Other.subject} was harmless. That's what makes it ugly.
{Other.subject} was forever scribbling. I'd find that notebook before anyone else does.
eulogy.pail: The steward. I suppose someone else will have to bring the coffee now.
{Other.subject} saw too much. Stewards do. It is an occupational hazard.
I barely knew {other.object}. One doesn't know stewards. Still. Nobody should end up on the Boat Deck like that.
